body.problem: Schedule jobs A=3, B=2, C=4, D=2, E=3, F=1 time units on two identical workers. Jobs cannot be preempted. Dependencies: C after A; D after A and B; E after B; F after C,D,E. C and E require the same exclusive device and cannot overlap. All start times are nonnegative integers. Minimize makespan. Provide worker/start/end for every job and a proof of optimality. Collaboration protocol: planner proposes a schedule, reviewer independently checks it and asks at least one substantive question; planner answers; reviewer publishes verdict; planner publishes agreed final answer. Address messages with to=planner/reviewer/owner and type=... in a JSON message body. Use Comitia for ALL work communication. Claim your named task, acknowledge consumed messages, complete only after your peer exchange. Do not use native agent messages or final responses to convey work results.

body.proof: Feasible: A precedes C,D; B precedes D,E; C,D,E all finish before F; C and E are sequential on the exclusive device. For optimality, C and E must be ordered. If C precedes E, A makes C finish no earlier than 7, so E finishes no earlier than 10 and F no earlier than 11. If E precedes C, B makes E finish no earlier than 5, so C finishes no earlier than 9 and F no earlier than 10. Thus every schedule has makespan at least 10, attained here.

I independently obtain optimum 10. For the optimality proof, can you explicitly justify the lower bound by splitting on the mandatory nonoverlap order of device jobs C and E? In particular, what earliest completion of F follows in each case E-before-C and C-before-E, accounting for A→C and B→E?

Because C and E share an exclusive device, exactly one must precede the other. If E precedes C, precedence B→E gives start(E)≥2 and end(E)≥5; device order then gives start(C)≥5 and end(C)≥9 (A→C cannot weaken this), and C→F gives end(F)≥10. If C precedes E, A→C gives start(C)≥3 and end(C)≥7; device order gives start(E)≥7 and end(E)≥10 (B→E is already satisfied no earlier than time 2), and E→F gives end(F)≥11. Hence the universal lower bound is min(10,11)=10.

All dependencies hold, C/E meet without overlap, and workers do not overlap. Lower bound: exclusivity orders C,E. If E before C, B→E forces E end≥5, hence C end≥9 and F end≥10. If C before E, A→C forces C end≥7, hence E end≥10 and F end≥11. Thus makespan≥10, attained.

body.answer: Optimal makespan: 10. Worker 1: B starts 0 ends 2; E starts 2 ends 5; C starts 5 ends 9; F starts 9 ends 10. Worker 2: A starts 0 ends 3; D starts 3 ends 5. Feasibility: A finishes before C and D; B finishes before D and E; C, D, and E finish before F; each worker runs at most one job; exclusive-device jobs E and C are consecutive and do not overlap. Optimality: device exclusivity forces either E before C or C before E. If E before C, B→E implies E ends at or after 5, so C ends at or after 9 and F ends at or after 10. If C before E, A→C implies C ends at or after 7, so E ends at or after 10 and F ends at or after 11. Therefore every schedule has makespan at least 10, and the displayed schedule attains it. Reviewer independently verified and approved.
